name: TESSERA SC-7 'Compliance'
description:
A handheld directed-energy stun device that delivers a calibrated electrical discharge through two barbed probes connected to the weapon by conductive microfilament wires. The SC-7 is TESSERA's flagship less-lethal sidearm, designed for corporate security personnel who need to incapacitate subjects without the liability of ballistic weapons. The device fires its probes at ranges up to 10 meters, and the electrical discharge is calibrated to cause involuntary muscle contraction and temporary incapacitation lasting 5-15 seconds depending on the target's body mass and augmentation level.

The 'calibrated' part is what distinguishes — and damns — the SC-7. The weapon's onboard processor analyzes the electrical impedance of the target's body through the probe connection and adjusts the discharge to maximize incapacitation while remaining below documented lethality thresholds. This sounds humane until you realize that the calibration database includes cyberware profiles — the SC-7 knows what augmentations the target has and adjusts its discharge to exploit their electrical characteristics. Against a heavily augmented target, the weapon doesn't just cause muscle contraction; it sends feedback spikes through cybernetic systems that cause the target's own implants to malfunction, creating pain responses and motor disruption far beyond what the electrical discharge alone would achieve.
legality: Licensed — corporate security and law enforcement
specifications:
range: 10 meters (probe delivery)
discharge: 50,000 volts, adaptive amperage
incapacitation duration: 5-15 seconds
probe type: Barbed titanium with microfilament tether
charges per cartridge: 3 firings
weight: 0.6 kg
length: 195mm
tactical_use: Subject incapacitation in corporate security operations, arrest support, and crowd control. Security teams use the SC-7 as a first-response tool before escalating to ballistic weapons. The cyberware exploitation feature makes it particularly effective against augmented targets who might otherwise resist conventional stun weapons.
cultural_context: The SC-7 is standard issue for corporate security across GLMZ, and its nickname 'Corporate Handshake' reflects public perception of how corponations greet people who disagree with them. The weapon's cyberware exploitation feature has drawn protests from augmentation rights groups who argue it constitutes targeted violence against the augmented community.
story_hooks: The SC-7's cyberware profiling database has been leaked, revealing that TESSERA has cataloged the electrical vulnerabilities of every major cyberware platform on the market — including experimental military augmentations that aren't supposed to exist in civilian populations.

A modified SC-7 has surfaced that inverts the calibration — instead of staying below lethality thresholds, it maximizes discharge through cyberware systems to cause permanent implant damage. Someone is turning a compliance tool into a cyberware destroyer.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, purpose-built stun device with a distinctly corporate aesthetic—angular and ergonomic, resembling a high-end taser crossed with a precision instrument. The silhouette is compact and predatory, with a pronounced grip section and a forward-tapering barrel assembly. It reads as 'clinical efficiency' at first glance: clean lines, minimal ornamentation, the look of something designed by committee to inflict compliance without appearing brutal.
physical_description.dimensions: 195mm length overall. Barrel assembly extends 65mm forward. Grip width approximately 35mm. Probe cartridge housing sits proud of the frame by roughly 15mm.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and surprisingly light in the hand—0.6kg feels almost insubstantial for a weapon, closer to a high-end power tool than a firearm. The weight distribution favors the grip, making it point-naturally. Feels precise rather than imposing.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer frame with titanium probe cartridge housing and conductive rail systems. Internal chassis of anodized aluminum for electrical conductivity and thermal dissipation.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with brushed titanium accents. The probe cartridge housing gleams with a professional silver finish. All conductive surfaces show deliberate brushwork to catch light without glare.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant charcoal-gray with silver-titanium accents. Small glowing elements: TESSERA branding in pale blue biolume, status LEDs positioned along the grip in amber and green.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with subtle crosshatch pattern for secure purchase even in wet conditions. Ergonomic finger grooves molded into the frame. The grip feels clinical—designed to fit many hand sizes but comfort secondary to control.
distinctive_features: Twin probe cartridge ports on forward assembly—visible as recessed titanium-ringed openings
Thin horizontal status LED strip running along the right grip side (amber for charging, green for ready, red for fault)
Conductive rail system visible as thin silver lines running the length of the frame—pathways for microfilament deployment
Miniature processor module visible through a small transparent port on the left side, showing faint blue circuitry
Target acquisition indicator: small LCD window displaying range and cyberware profile data in monochrome text
Cartridge counter etched into the grip—shows remaining probe loads
Subtle TESSERA serial plate inset flush into the grip pommel
Heat vents on the rear grip—small angled slots for thermal management during rapid discharge
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA logo (geometric T) embossed in glossy finish on the grip, approximately 40mm from the pommel. Serial plate inset flush into grip base. 'SC-7 COMPLIANCE' etched in small sans-serif font along the barrel. Safety certification marks stamped on the frame's left side. Product serial number laser-etched on the heat sink assembly.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained and clinical. Corporate security weapons rarely show wear—they're regularly serviced and kept clean. Surface shows only minor signs of field use: light scratches on the polymer, faint discoloration where hands grip repeatedly, occasional dust residue in the vent slots. The overall impression is 'professional tool in active use' rather than battle-worn.
